title: Grounds of Suspension and the Route Back for a Keyturn Vehicle Listing
content:
A Keyturn Vehicle Listing is suspended for a stated ground and never without one, the grounds being an overdue inspection, an expired registration, a safety defect, an open recall, a valuation outside the class band, a policy breach and the host's own request. The ground stands on the marketplace's own record of the listing before the suspension takes effect, and is gathered to the vehicle by the listing it is recorded against; a listing may be suspended out of the review, live, snoozed or suspended standings and out of no other.

A suspension takes the vehicle off the calendar at once, and where the ground is a safety defect, an open recall or an expired registration it also ends the bookings already confirmed on that vehicle, the guests being treated as cancelled on by the marketplace rather than by the host.

A suspended listing may be put back inside the class's reinstatement window, counted in whole calendar days from the day of suspension, once the ground has been put right and evidenced; reinstatement is reviewed within the class's review period in business days. The window is read off the day of suspension standing on the marketplace's record of that listing, and the comparison is a not-later-than: a request made on the last day of the window is inside it.

*On the boundary.* A class whose reinstatement window is 45 calendar days: a request made on the 45th calendar day after the day of suspension is inside the window; one made on the 46th is not.

The host may appeal a suspension inside the class's appeal period, and an appeal does not put the vehicle back on the calendar while it is decided, because the ground of suspension stands until it is overturned.

A listing taken down for good is delisted on the class's notice, and delisting ends the protection enrolment on that vehicle as well, since protection follows the listing and does not outlive it.

A listing whose reinstatement window has passed is delisted rather than left suspended, and the host who wants the vehicle back lists it afresh and is reviewed as a new listing.
